stem: A 44-year-old woman comes to the office due to intermittent right upper quadrant discomfort that is brought on by fatty meals.  She has lost 14 kg (31 lb) over the past 4 months through a strict low-calorie diet.  Vital signs are normal.  Abdominal examination shows mild right upper quadrant tenderness without guarding.  Murphy sign is negative.  Ultrasonography reveals a small gallstone in the gallbladder.  There is no wall edema or pericholecystic fluid and the bile ducts are normal caliber.  After discussion of treatment options, the patient prefers medical therapy with ursodiol.  This medication is most likely to improve this patient's condition via which of the following mechanisms?​‌​‌​​​‌‌​​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​​​​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​​​‌‌​‌​‌​‌‌‌​​‌‌​​​‌‌​​​​​‌​‌‌​​​‌​​‌​‌‌​​​‌‌​​​‌​​‌​​‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌​‌​​‌‌​​‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌​‌‌‌‌‌​​​‌​‌​​‌​​‌‌​​​​‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌​​‌​‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌​‌​​​‌‌​‌‌​​​​‌‌​‌​‌​​‌‌​​‌​‌‌​‌‌‌​​‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌‌‌​​‌‌‌​​‌‌​‌​​​​​‌‌​​​​‌​‌​‌​​‌​​​‌​‌‌​​‌‌​​​‌‌​​‌‌‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌​​​‌‌​‌​‌‌​​‌​​‌​​​​​‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌​​​​

options.label: A
options.text: Blocks HMG-CoA reductase to reduce hepatic cholesterol synthesis

options.label: B
options.text: Decreases biliary cholesterol secretion and increases bile acid content

options.label: C
options.text: Increases biliary phospholipid secretion to dissolve gallstones

options.label: D
options.text: Inhibits intestinal cholesterol absorption via blockade of the NPC1L1 transporter

options.label: E
options.text: Stimulates lipoprotein lipase synthesis to enhance triglyceride clearance

explanation:
Cholesterol gallstones form when bile becomes supersaturated with cholesterol, causing the cholesterol to precipitate and crystallize.  Rapid weight loss, as seen in this patient, is a well-recognized risk factor because it increases cholesterol mobilization and secretion into the bile while slowing gallbladder emptying, tipping the balance toward lithogenesis.  This patient's biliary colic symptoms, along with the absence of ductal dilation, lack of fever, and negative Murphy sign, are consistent with uncomplicated cholelithiasis, which is sometimes managed medically with ursodiol in patients who prefer to avoid or have contraindications to surgery.

Ursodiol (ursodeoxycholic acid) decreases biliary cholesterol secretion and expands the hydrophilic bile acid pool, thereby increasing cholesterol solubility in bile.  Together, these actions make bile less lithogenic and allow existing cholesterol crystals to gradually dissolve over months of therapy.  Ursodiol is effective only for cholesterol stones, not for pigment stones.

(Choice A)  Statins inhibit HMG-CoA reductase to reduce systemic cholesterol synthesis; although statins lower circulating cholesterol, they do not meaningfully alter bile composition or dissolve gallstones.

(Choice C)  Phospholipids do contribute to cholesterol solubilization in bile, but ursodiol acts by decreasing biliary cholesterol secretion and expanding the bile acid pool rather than by altering phospholipid secretion.

(Choice D)  Ezetimibe blocks the Niemann-Pick C1–like 1 (NPC1L1) transporter in the small intestine to reduce cholesterol absorption but has no direct effect on biliary cholesterol secretion and does not promote stone dissolution.

(Choice E)  Fibrates are PPAR-alpha agonists that increase lipoprotein lipase expression to enhance triglyceride clearance.  They are used in hypertriglyceridemia, not gallstone disease, and in fact increase the risk of cholesterol gallstone formation.

Educational objective:Ursodiol dissolves cholesterol gallstones by reducing biliary cholesterol secretion and expanding the bile acid pool, making bile less saturated.  It can be used for medical management of uncomplicated cholesterol cholelithiasis in patients who prefer to avoid or have contraindications to surgery.​‌​‌​​​‌‌​​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​​​​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​​​‌‌​‌​‌​‌‌‌​​‌‌​​​‌‌​​​​​‌​‌‌​​​‌​​‌​‌‌​​​‌‌​​​‌​​‌​​‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌​‌​​‌‌​​‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌​‌‌‌‌‌​​​‌​‌​​‌​​‌‌​​​​‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌​​‌​‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌​‌​​​‌‌​‌‌​​​​‌‌​‌​‌​​‌‌​​‌​‌‌​‌‌‌​​‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌‌‌​​‌‌‌​​‌‌​‌​​​​​‌‌​​​​‌​‌​‌​​‌​​​‌​‌‌​​‌‌​​​‌‌​​‌‌‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌​​​‌‌​‌​‌‌​​‌​​‌​​​​​‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌​​​​
